locator: I q.2 a.3 co., secunda via: in omnibus causis efficientibus ordinatis, primum est causa medii, et medium est causa ultimi
interpretation: Reading A (strong), parallel to the prima via's AQUINAS-ST-I-Q2-A3-SECOND-MOVERS-A: an efficient cause other than its effect that is itself efficiently caused in any respect is a middle cause, causing only as caused. 'Remota autem causa, removetur effectus' is read as the reason why the middle's causing depends on its cause. All predicates are present (simul), so a per accidens series of past generations (ST I q.46 a.2 ad 7, reading A) is not a counterexample; but presentness does not settle a cause caused now in an irrelevant respect, which reading B (AQUINAS-ST-I-Q2-A3-SECOND-EFFICIENT-CAUSES-B) does not make a middle cause. Result AQUINAS-ST-I-Q2-A3-SECUNDA-VIA is conditional on this strong reading; its countermodels show the encoded premise is needed, not that this reading is the faithful one.
